claims.text: Percolative, ordered B2-like HfTi and TiZr clusters form in HfNbTaTiZr.
The ordered binary clusters reduce local lattice-distortion amplitude relative to the random solid solution.
Reduced lattice distortion shifts the high-frequency phonon DOS to higher frequencies.
The ordering-induced reduction in distortion lowers phonon-scattering rates and produces a net increase in lattice thermal conductivity.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr material is a random solid solution.
HfNbTaTiZr has a thermal conductivity of approximately 10–17 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹.
Lattice distortion and defects in HfNbTaTiZr depress electron and phonon propagation and contribute to its low thermal conductivity.
Thermal annealing or controlled cooling can induce percolative HfTi and TiZr B2-like SRO while retaining the overall BCC matrix.
A treatment at 600–1000 °C is sufficient to drive the proposed order-disorder transition in HfNbTaTiZr.
Quenching after ordering preserves the proposed SRO.
The ordered cluster network locally regularizes atomic positions and reduces atomic-radius and lattice-parameter fluctuations.
SRO flattens the potential-energy landscape relevant to high-frequency phonons.
A high-frequency DOS blueshift increases phonon group velocities and lifetimes.
Percolating ordered clusters create low-resistance phonon-transport pathways whose benefit outweighs scattering at cluster boundaries.
The ordered sample will have lattice thermal conductivity exceeding 17 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹.
The ordered sample will exhibit higher-frequency phonon-DOS peaks than the random alloy.
Mean-square atomic displacements will be lower within the ordered regions.
A conductivity increase occurs only when the ordered clusters form a percolating network.
Isolated precipitates or a continuous brittle intermetallic phase instead decrease conductivity through interface scattering.
The proposed conductivity enhancement is limited to the high-frequency phonon regime in which lattice distortion dominates scattering.
